coverage.governance_rule: DISCOVERY COVERAGE ≠ EVIDENCE COVERAGE ≠ FAMILY COVERAGE

ownership_graph.question: What does CereVasc own?
ownership_graph.answer: 147 patents discovered via P005 assignee search. 87 claim-audited. 25 US granted (all Active). 41 failed to retrieve (mostly JP/CN/DE foreign — claims not in PatSnap).

technology_graph.question: What technology does CereVasc know/use?
technology_graph.answer: CereVasc knows: (1) endovascular CSF shunt deployment, (2) dural venous sinus access, (3) shunt valve design, (4) anti-occlusion coating, (5) patency verification via contrast agent + imaging (EP3212275A1), (6) delivery systems, (7) anatomical mapping with ultrasound/OCT sensors. CereVasc does NOT know: continuous pressure monitoring, pressure differential measurement, predictive occlusion algorithm, wireless implantable telemetry for shunt.
technology_graph.key_finding: EP3212275A1 — CereVasc has patency verification via contrast agent + imaging. This is the closest existing IP to RESCUE_001.

buyer_graph.question: What technical capability is commercially valuable but not protected?
buyer_graph.answer: CONTINUOUS, IN-VIVO, ENDOGENOUS pressure-based patency monitoring. CereVasc has periodic, exogenous, contrast-agent-based verification. The gap is: continuous monitoring without contrast injection, using the eShunt anatomy to create a CSF-venous pressure differential signal.
buyer_graph.rationale: CereVasc recognized the patency problem and solved it with contrast agent + imaging. The next step (continuous, endogenous, predictive) is NOT in their portfolio. But the motivation to verify patency IS present, increasing 103 risk.

PROTECTED_CORE.description: Core eShunt technology — CSF drainage method, shunt design, deployment system
PROTECTED_CORE.strength: STRONG — foundational patents for endovascular CSF shunt

PROTECTED_ADJACENT.strength: STRONG — continuation family protecting delivery/access methods

KNOWN_BUT_UNPROTECTED.description: Patency verification via contrast agent + imaging — CereVasc knows this technique and has patented it, but it requires exogenous contrast injection
KNOWN_BUT_UNPROTECTED.strength: MODERATE — patented but uses different mechanism from RESCUE_001
KNOWN_BUT_UNPROTECTED.key_insight: CereVasc already recognized the patency problem. They solved it with contrast agent + imaging. The UNSOLVED problem is: continuous monitoring without contrast injection.

COMPETITOR_DENSE.description: Implantable pressure sensors, wireless telemetry, ICP monitoring — thousands of competitor patents exist
COMPETITOR_DENSE.strength: DENSE — the general sensing space is heavily patented. But endovascular CSF-venous differential is specific.
COMPETITOR_DENSE.rationale: No killer patent (L5+L6) found in 15 most similar patents. The space is dense but the specific combination (CSF-venous differential + predictive algorithm + endovascular context) has not been found.

EMERGING_TECHNOLOGY.description: Ultrasound/OCT sensors for anatomical mapping during deployment
EMERGING_TECHNOLOGY.strength: EMERGING — sensors for navigation, not yet for monitoring

UNOCCUPIED_TECHNICAL_TERRITORY.description: CONTINUOUS, IN-VIVO, ENDOGENOUS pressure-differential-based patency monitoring with predictive algorithm
UNOCCUPIED_TECHNICAL_TERRITORY.strength: UNOCCUPIED — no CereVasc patent and no competitor patent found in the similar set
UNOCCUPIED_TECHNICAL_TERRITORY.key_limitation: L1+L2+L3+L5 combination (CSF pressure + venous pressure + differential + occlusion prediction) not found in ANY audited patent

HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.description: The specific territory where RESCUE_001 would operate
HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.definition: A system that continuously monitors CSF shunt patency by measuring the pressure differential between CSF and venous blood, using the eShunt anatomical configuration, and predicting occlusion before clinical symptoms — WITHOUT requiring contrast agent injection or imaging.
differentiation_from_existing: CONTINUOUS vs periodic (EP3212275A1 requires contrast injection each time)
ENDOGENOUS vs exogenous (pressure signal is always present, contrast agent must be injected)
PREDICTIVE vs detection (algorithm predicts occlusion before it happens, imaging only detects after)
NON-INVASIVE vs invasive (no contrast injection needed after deployment)
HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.buyer_value: HIGH — CereVasc needs post-market surveillance data for PMA; continuous monitoring reduces revision surgeries; differentiates from VP shunt competitors
HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.technical_differentiation: MODERATE — the CSF-venous differential is a new signal enabled by eShunt anatomy
HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.patentability: UNCERTAIN — 102 survives but 103 is uncertain due to CereVasc existing patency IP
HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.defensibility: MEDIUM — competitors could use flow sensing or imaging instead
HIGH_VALUE_WHITE_SPACE.strategic_importance: HIGH — could become platform patent extending beyond the shunt itself

rescue_001_final_assessment.102: SURVIVES — no single reference discloses all 6 limitations (L1-L6)
rescue_001_final_assessment.103: UNCERTAIN — CereVasc has patency verification IP (EP3212275A1) using contrast agent + imaging. The question: would a PHOSITA have reason to replace exogenous contrast/imaging with endogenous pressure differential? The mechanisms are different but the motivation (patency verification) is present in CereVasc portfolio.
evidence_gaps: 41 foreign patents still not claim-audited (JP/CN/DE — PatSnap does not have their claims)
53 similar patents found but only 15 claim-checked
10 physical-mechanism searches returned thousands of results — not claim-level searched
External prior art (non-CereVasc) not systematically claim-searched for the specific L1+L2+L3+L5 combination
next_steps: Patent counsel opinion on 103 obviousness over EP3212275A1
Physical validation of CSF-venous differential concept
Consider whether a DIFFERENT invention (derived from moat map) might be more defensible

invention_strategy.current: RESCUE_001 — CSF-venous pressure differential + occlusion prediction
alternative_directions_from_moat_map: OCCLUSION PREVENTION (not prediction) — structural design to prevent occlusion (CereVasc has US20260224866A1 in this space but only for arachnoid layer)
FLOW REGULATION — active flow control based on pressure feedback (CereVasc has valve but not active control)
DRUG DELIVERY — CereVasc website mentions blood-brain barrier delivery; eShunt anatomy enables drug delivery to CSF
RETRIEVAL/RESCUE — system for removing or repositioning a failed eShunt (CereVasc has delivery but not retrieval)
PATIENT SELECTION — imaging/anatomy assessment for eShunt candidacy (CereVasc has US20250228618A1 for planning but not AI-based selection)
invention_strategy.recommendation: Consider whether RESCUE_001 (pressure monitoring) or a moat-map-derived alternative (e.g., flow regulation, retrieval, or drug delivery) has better patentability + buyer value + defensibility. The moat map shows that monitoring is the NARROWEST white space (CereVasc already has contrast-agent-based patency verification). Other directions may have WIDER white space.
